messages.subject: Clustering on PCA data
messages.body_plain:
Fist, sorry if the answer is trivial. Proficient in Delpgi, but just started R today. I am really glad I found your Cardinal package.

So: my R code
- loads the Analyze file to data
- normalizes data to data2
- runs PCA on data2, say PC1-PC15, and puts them into data3
- I would like to run spatialKMeans on data3 and put them to data4 but get an error message:

> data4 <- spatialKMeans(data3, r=2, k=15, method="adaptive")
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘spatialKMeans’ for signature ‘"PCA"’

Can you help me?

Many thanks in advance, Vilmos

messages.subject: Re: Clustering on PCA data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vilmos,

You should run spatialKMeans or spatialShrunkenCentroids on "data2", which is the actual dataset, not on "data3" which is simply the results of PCA.

If you really want to do spatial k-means on the PC scores, you could create a new image dataset that uses the PC scores as the data.

data4 <- SImageSet(data=t(data3$scores[[1]]), coord=coord(data2))
data5 <- spatialKMeans(data4, r=2, k=15)

However, the clustering would not be any better than if you just did spatial k-means on "data2" in the first place.

Furthermore, if you do spatialShrunkenCentroids, a major goal of the method is to allow interpretation of the t-statistics for each m/z feature. The t-statistics would not be as meaningful if they corresponded to the PC's instead.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: filter by intensity
messages.body_plain:
The simplest way to do that while plotting an image is to use the 'zlim' argument.

image(msset, mz=443, zlim=c(100,200))

That does require you set the upper range manually, though. If you need a way to do it without specifying the upper range manually, you can do:

image(msset, mz=443, subset=spectra(msset)[features(msset, mz=443),] >= 100)

If you want to filter all intensities and save it as a new dataset, you could do that via a custom normalization method:

msset2 <- normalize(msset, method=function(x) ifelse(x > 7, x, 0))

-Kylie

messages.subject: Error while performing normalization
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kylie,

I am using Cardinal to work with a MSI dataset available on the PRIDE database (PXD001283). This dataset is in preprocessed *.imzML format. So, first I converted it to continuous format using the SpectralAnalysis tool (https://github.com/AlanRace/SpectralAnalysis).

I am able to work with this dataset without applying any prepossessing steps. However, while trying to perform normalization, I get this error:

> normalize(HRData_C_CAR, pixel = 1, method = "tic", plot = TRUE)
normalize: Using method = tic
Error in if (auc > 0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Smoothing the data works. But then, on trying to perform baseline correction, I get the following error:

> reduceBaseline(HRData_C_CAR, pixel=1, method="median", blocks=50, plot=TRUE)
reduceBaseline: Using method = median
Error in baseidx + c(0, cumsum(sapply(xint, length))[-length(xint)]) :
  non-numeric argument to binary operator

I am not sure whats causing these errors. But I assume it to be related to some format issues with the converted continuous *.imzML file.
Can you maybe give some hint?

Many thanks,
Purva
